 Most recent Most popular 'The boys were excellent' published at 18:31 GMT 18:31 GMT 
 FT: Hull City 2-2 Ipswich Town 
 Ipswich Town 
 Ipswich Town boss Gary O'Neil, speaking to Match of the Day, said: "We were the better side, we should have punished them more in the first half. We gifted them two goals, then we responded unbelievable well.
 "The goals [we conceded] were the only real disappointing part, a lot of errors for goals which has cost us but in terms of coming away from home, dominating the game, defending, attacking, I thought the lads were very good today.
 "We knew they [Hull] would change [at half-time] and they were better than in the first half but they still were not better than us, we were the better team. It's a point on the road and I've watched a lot of Hull's games and not a lot of teams were as good with the ball as we were.
 "It's tough to go away from home, we keep moving forwards and get ourselves ready for Bournemouth in the next one. The boys were excellent and mistakes will happen and it's just unfortunate that the only two errors we made both led to goals - I didn't like either of their two goals and the second one is preventable.
 "I'm really pleased with where my team is at after that today. We were the better team away from home and that takes some doing. It's tough to be in control and find yourselves 2-1 down with the place bouncing. Our lads have some character and we just need to keep it up. Hull are a very good side and I'm really pleased with how we did against them."

 'Nothing to moan about' published at 18:29 GMT 18:29 GMT 
 FT: Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds 
 Leeds United 
 Leeds boss Daniel Farke, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "Football can sometimes be tough and one of the most unfair sports in the world. Very often, just one goal is decisive and even though you should win or not lose, you can lose such a game. A terrific first half performance, scored fantastic goals and just with a margin ruled out. We could be more clinical and then out of nothing we scored more or less an own goal. If they are then 1-0 up they have the home crowd and it's also difficult. How strong they are they've proven over the last two months. Then they scored another.
 "It's tough for the boys because performance-wise, nothing to moan about. Sometimes you have to accept a loss. The team was a bit more clinical and for that, congratulations to Bournemouth."
 On the first goal: "Wrong decision. We are a side that doesn't just put the ball long. It's like an own goal out of nothing so it gave the belief to the stadium. If you make a mistake you can also lose a game. We're all human beings. We should have done better but it happens."
 On whether it took belief away from Leeds: "It's normal because we should be in the lead and we spoke before about how difficult it is away at Bournemouth. Then you feel a bit sorry for yourself and it's important that you then react quickly. It's a bit more difficult but this happens sometimes. You have to deal with setbacks. For a few moments, it was more a bit of disbelief but we're all in this game for so long, we've all seen it happen."
 On the disallowed goal: "I haven't watched it back. I was thinking we scored, if there was a handball, we have to accept it."
 On their lack of chances: "If one team is defending so deep and sometimes you need to force a goal, we could've been a bit more on it. It's definitely something we could've done better. It's more or less the only criticism."
 3 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Players fought until the end' published at 18:28 GMT 18:28 GMT 
 FT: Man City 0-1 Brighton 
 Manchester City 
 Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca speaking to BBC MOTD: 
 "A bit strange. The same feeling as after Aston Villa away. We did enough to deserve something more but we have to move on and try to win games.
 "We created a good volume of offensive action. Sometimes you have to be more clinical and score but it's important that we create.
 "We did everything to be honest. Sometimes you struggle to score and the important thing is we created the chances. The attitude was good, I have nothing to say about that or the performance. Players fought until the end and hopefully next time we are more lucky."
 10 40 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Belief key to winning these games' published at 18:27 GMT 18:27 GMT 
 FT: Man City 0-1 Brighton 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Image source, Getty Images Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler speaking to BBC MOTD: 
 "Really happy for everyone involved. A long journey, everyone contributed to the win. Really happy who the did the work in the shadows and we showed another good performance on the pitch. Togetherness gives us the rewards. On Wednesday we missed the luck, today we had a bit of luck but you have to deserve the luck and everyone worked hard for today.
 "It was a completely defensive performance where everyone had the mindset 'I need to defend'. We would have preferred to have more of the ball but in certain moments you know when you come here you need to suffer and defend well in the box. We can talk about individual players but in the end everyone had a defensive mindset and stuck together."
 On belief in squad and Bart Verbruggen providing stability: "Football is a lot about belief. You need to have players who spread that belief and Bart is a prime example of that. But they all have this belief that are capable of coming here and competing and winning these games. It's important to have this mindset and to spread it around the environment we work in and belief is key to winning these types of games.
 "Coming here to City against one of the best teams in the league is always special. You have to be brilliant at the basics and everyone was contributing, from Tuesday when we travelled and we wanted to have a good four days and enjoy it and finish strong. Everyone can enjoy this win today."

 " VAR: “Point of contact is on the achilles, nowhere near the ball. He’s sprinting at speed and with intensity, the studs catch him flush on the achilles. I think it ticks all the boxes for serious foul play”.
